existing.description: The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) is a University of Amsterdam award for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA who apply for a degree programme at the university. Applications are handled by the Admissions Offices of the Graduate Schools, and deadlines, eligibility requirements and selection criteria differ per faculty. The award is a grant and not a tuition waiver: the Faculty of Science states the recipient must still pay the full tuition fee and that the grant is paid in monthly instalments. The Faculty of Science publishes one AMS of EUR 26,125 for the September 2027 start with a 15 January deadline.
eligibility: Hold a non-EU/EEA passport (Faculty of Science also excludes Suisse nationality)
Not eligible for support under the Dutch system of study grants and loans (Studiefinanciering)
Not eligible for the reduced EEA tuition fee rate at the UvA
Not in receipt of another full-coverage scholarship for the same period of study
Submit a complete application to a UvA master's programme and be admitted for the first time
Be able to comply with Dutch visa regulations
Have completed the previous academic programme no longer than three years ago (Faculty of Science)
Have sufficient funds to cover all other costs
existing.eligibility_summary: Students holding a non-EU/EEA passport who have applied for an eligible degree programme at the University of Amsterdam and who are not eligible for Dutch study financing or reduced EEA tuition.
benefits: Monthly instalments of the scholarship amount (Faculty of Science)
Second-year continuation for two-year master's programmes at the Faculty of Science if at least 40 ECTS are passed
coverage: Cash grant sized by the awarding Graduate School; the Faculty of Science publishes EUR 26,125 for the September 2027 start
Not usable as a tuition fee waiver - the recipient still pays the full tuition fee
No living-cost, housing or travel coverage
requirements: Submit the AMS request as part of the master's programme application
Tick the scholarship option on the application form
Meet the specific Graduate School selection criteria and deadlines
existing.english_requirement: The central AMS page sets no English requirement; the individual Graduate School and master's programme set the language requirements (for example the Psychology Graduate School requires IELTS 7.0, TOEFL 100 iBT or Cambridge C1 Advanced 190).
application_method: Apply for the relevant UvA master's programme
In the application form indicate that you wish to be considered for a UvA scholarship / the AMS
Upload any additional materials the Graduate School requires (for example a motivation letter)
existing.selection_notes: Selection criteria are set per Graduate School and generally include academic excellence, the quality of the motivation letter and, for some faculties, a lottery among eligible applicants.
existing.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants with a top-decile academic record who are applying to a UvA master's programme and can demonstrate strong motivation and cover their own living costs.
existing.notes: The number of awards and the amount differ per faculty or Graduate School, so the award is a family of faculty-level funds rather than one centrally funded scholarship. The stored uva.nl URL for this record is dead; the current central page is under Fees and funding > Master's scholarships and loans.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the September intake. Applications are made as part of the master's programme application, so they open with the relevant master's admissions round and close at the faculty deadline.
existing.deadline_display: Faculty-specific: "Deadlines for the AMS differ per Faculty or Graduate School." The Faculty of Science states "The application deadline is 15 January"; other Graduate Schools publish different dates (for example 1 March for Psychology and 2 February for Social Sciences).
existing.program_type: University merit scholarship, awarded per faculty or Graduate School
